x: Quackenbos, our Junior Captain, had an excellent throw of 12ft. 9in. and was actually placed 7th. L. Jackson had an off day, after throwing over 120 ft. consistently on practice.

We have some very useful runners in our Junior ranks and with careful and regular training they should prove useful assets to our senior sides as they grow older. The Javelin Throw handicap was won by L. Jackson, who is our field events vice-captain.

Cambridge H. our men were first and third in the High Jump (Quackenbos and Marchant); first and fourth in the Discus (Sutton and Jackson); first and fourth in Javelin (Quackenbos and Jackson); and second and fourth in the Long Jump (Skelley and "Q").
We have a new Field Events Captain in Charlie Jones, who will receive capable assistance from L. Jackson, W.

Both Syd Jones and Laurie Jackson also helped us when on leave. Outstanding performances of the season were Syd Jones's shot putt of 38ft. 11in. and Bill Sutton's 36ft. 1in. in the same match at Enfield; Ford's high jump of 5ft. 8in. at Tooting on the eve of his joining the Forces; Melchoir's javeli…
Lawrence Jackson, writing from South Devon, says, " Oh! for the good times of old to return, Club runs, socials, etc." Managed to win the shot putt on Sports Day.
Laurie Jackson (Jacko) writing from Bishop Auckland, says:—"I'm still keeping well and am looking forward to a return to activity with the Field Events Section."
Margaret O'Kell, Norman Graves, Jack Field, Laurie Jackson, Frank Elson, Joe Coleman, Ted Jury, Mr. and Mrs. Dick Murphy, John Frost, "Lillian" (bless her heart!), Hon.

Laurie Jackson writes from Folkestone "Wishing all members a very Happy New Year, and may 1944 bring Peace!" He has been transferred from the "Buffs" to the "Die Hards." Frequently hears from Bill Sutton and they intend to have the railings by the putting circle or the track, at Battersea Park, shif…

Laurie Jackson was wounded in Normandy by shrapnel from a mortar bomb, and spent a time in hospital at Bradford. His last copy of the mag. has a large hole in it—it was in his pocket when he stopped his "packet." We'll try and get the next copy on bullet-proof paper!
Harley, Charlie Cook, "Megaphone Man" Cook, Harry Churcher, Jack Carne, Jack Field, Bill Jones, Laurie Jackson, Bill Lucas, George Long, Bert ("Champ") and Mrs.
Bill True is still busy at Sandhurst, but was able to visit us and turn out at the Open Walk. Laurie Jackson is still undergoing treatment and is having a skin grafting at the back of his knee.
Laurie Jackson was at the Club Handicap Meeting, and was still limping. George Tyrer, our oldest cross-country runner, looked in at the Hall recently.
Laurie Jackson has recently become a proud father, and we have great pleasure in announcing the election to the Club of Master Roger Jackson.
The Field Event handicaps were well supported and Bill Sutton and Syd Jones were among the prize-winners, and it was pleasing to see Laurie Jackson gaining a first award.

LAURIE JACKSON was wounded in Normandy by shrapnel from a mortar bomb and spent a time in hospital at Bradford. His last copy of the "Belgravian" has a large hole in it---it was in his pocket when he stopped his "packet".
